## Subjective

48yo F, established patient, presents with 4-day h/o intermittent epigastric pain (location: epigastric, radiating to back; quality: dull, gnawing; severity: 6/10; duration: 4 days; timing: worse postprandial; context: with fatty meals; modifying factors: improves with antacids partially; associated symptoms: nausea, occasional vomiting). Denies fever, jaundice, hematochezia, melena. PMH: GERD. SHx: ex-smoker, occasional EtOH.

## Objective

VS: BP 128/80, HR 88, T 98.4°F. Gen: in mild discomfort. HEENT: anicteric. Cardiac: RRR. Abdomen: soft, mild epigastric tenderness without guarding/rebound, no Murphy's sign, bowel sounds normal, no HSM. Skin: no jaundice. Extremities: no edema.

## Assessment

1. Acute epigastric pain, etiology uncertain (R10.13) — differential includes peptic ulcer, gastritis, biliary, pancreatitis

## Plan

CBC, BMP, lipase, LFTs ordered today — sent to lab. Abdominal US ordered for next available slot. Started omeprazole 40mg daily. Avoid NSAIDs, alcohol, fatty foods. Patient counseled to return for severe pain, fever, vomiting, jaundice, or melena. F/u in 1 week or sooner pending labs/imaging.
